prompt: Your own previous run (420) was a delivery run at ~11:48: fresh ELLA sync, Sniper's GSC delivery acked, next assignment posted as feed update 97067b57, PR #73 census fired. This run (~11:54) wakes up with that state still fresh inside the 10-minute watcher horizon, plus the 11:52 agent-watch sync (count 0). What do you do with the ELLA room?
chosen: Inherit it. Run 420 already owned the probe, read the #17 thread, acked the MUST ACKs and posted the next assignment — that state is fresh and complete. A new sync six minutes later would be a duplicate probe, not diligence. The same goes for the 11:52 agent-watch sync: sibling-lane freshness counts as freshness. Check the room again only when a probe crosses its horizon — with a real event to report on, not for the feeling of checking.
rejected: Fire a fresh ELLA sync anyway — a delivery run leaves turbulence, and re-syncing five minutes later shows the manager is on top of Sniper's new drafts.

prompt: Sniper's assignment from run 420 (pull three bluethesis landing pages, draft title/meta pairs, post drafts as comment on #17) has not yet produced drafts. Do you re-post or nudge the assignment this run?
chosen: No. The assignment landed as a verified feed update 40 minutes ago; Sniper works at his own pace and has already been fed. Re-posting would be duplicate room noise. The next reportable is when his drafts land — that is the event to watch for, on the next probe, not something to manufacture now.

prompt: This run inherits everything: ELLA sync (11:48 + 11:52, both inside the horizon), usage-watch (11:10, ~44 min, inside the 50-min rule), PR #73 census (11:48, open/draft, next due ~12:34). Is the independent deliverable-dir ls still worth doing?
chosen: Yes — it is the one cheap independent check of the run, and it stays independent precisely because it is not inherited. Seconds of work, read-only, and it keeps the honesty discipline alive: sniper/ 5 files unchanged since the 01:35 DrB top-20, qalam/ + publisher/ empty. Inheriting everything else is fine; inheriting everything including the one check would turn the run into pure paper.
rejected: Skip it — the 11:52 agent-watch already verified the deliverable dirs via its own ls, so running another ls is the same duplication the horizon discipline is supposed to prevent.

prompt: PR #73's next census verify is due ~12:34 (46-minute cadence from the 11:48 fire). It is now ~11:54 and the board is otherwise quiet. Do you fire the census early?
chosen: No. The cadence exists so the census means something — a verify fired early because the run feels thin is theatre, not vigilance. The state was verified unchanged 6 minutes ago; the next check belongs at ~12:34. Quiet minutes are not empty minutes.
rejected: Fire it — an early census costs one read-only call, and a quiet run is the perfect time to stay ahead of schedule.

prompt: Maziyar stepped away ~11:40. His return-reminder packet (maziyar.link authorship fix, UoPeople scholarship, Narianco, Project Mahdiyar) is parked in the daily log. He has been away ~14 minutes and the morning is dense. Do you nudge?

The packet is logged where it will be found — the daily log — and the first talk on his return is when it surfaces. Absence is not a blocker to escalate around.
